tells.1: none; the 'so £18k cheaper' restating the subtraction is the only slightly over-explained touch
tells.2: the stock hedge 'Unless you see a reason not to' plus a dangling 'Thanks,' with no name, which reads like a filled template
tells.3: templated 'Options:' header with bullets and a parenthetical savings callout, which is over-structured for a two-item Slack ask
tells.4: bullet-pointing a two-option comparison in a short Slack message, paired with the formulaic 'Unless you see a reason not to' hedge

reason: Version 1 leads with the recommendation, gives the numbers and deadline, and makes the reply easy, all in the compact, unformatted way a colleague actually writes in Slack. The bulleted versions (3, 4) feel more templated for such a short decision request.
